newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cabinet lifts foreign investment bans.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cabinet lifts foreign investment bans.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Monday lifted a ban restricting repatriation of income generated by foreign investments of less than $50,000 in a bid to boost investment in the crisis-ridden country.
"After the cabinet lifted this ban all foreign investments will be treated as such regardless of their size," a government's spokesman told reporters.

Under an amendment to the foreign investment law passed two years ago by the former socialist government, only foreign investments higher than the $50,000 threshold were entitled to repatriation of profits

Eliminating foreign investment restrictions is part of Bulgaria's reform pledges to the International Monetary Fund, which is expected to discuss the disbursement of second $130 million tranche on Wednesday.
The cabinet also lifted a restriction ruling that foreigners could not buy government paper with maturity shorter than six months.
The cabinet is expected to discuss more amendments to the foreign investment law on Thursday, which then will have to be passed in parliament.

Bulgaria has the lowest level of foreign investment in the region, less than one billion dollars so far. Inconsistent legislation, reluctant privatisation and excessive red tape have turned many investors away.
But the new reformist government pledged to speed up sell- offs, hoping to cover vast budget gaps with privatisation proceeds.
